proposals.title: Recover IBC light client for Injective (07-tendermint-0)
proposals.summary: This proposal updates the expired IBC light client `07-tendermint-0` for counterparty chain `injective-1` with the state of the substitute client `07-tendermint-8`. This revives transfer/channel-0 to Injective transfer/channel-436, which holds ~35,417 XRP in escrow.

proposals.title: Disable the Interchain Accounts Host Module
proposals.summary: This proposal disables the ICS-27 Interchain Accounts (ICA) host submodule by setting host_enabled to false and clearing its allow list. The module is being deprecated: it is not part of the chain's actively supported feature set and is not in use. Disabling it removes an unused module surface and simplifies node configuration and maintenance. The ICA controller submodule is not enabled on this chain, so this action fully disables Interchain Accounts. The change is reversible through a future governance proposal should the functionality be needed again.

proposals.title: XRPL EVM v9.0.0: Migration from Evmos to Cosmos EVM v0.4.2
proposals.summary:
The XRPL EVM sidechain chain upgrade v9.0.0 is ready to migrate Evmos—an unmaintained dependency—to Cosmos EVM v0.4.2, a fully supported fork of Evmos.
This is more than just a technical upgrade. By moving to Cosmos EVM, the XRPL EVM ecosystem gains:
 - Long-term sustainability: Evmos had become unsupported, leaving chains that depended on it without a clear upgrade path. Cosmos EVM is actively maintained, ensuring compatibility with the broader Cosmos and Ethereum ecosystems.
 - Future-proof development: Cosmos EVM continuously integrates Ethereum standards (EIPs) and protocol upgrades. This ensures that XRPL EVM applications remain interoperable with Ethereum tooling.
 - Extended functionality: The migration introduces new ERC-20 capabilities such as mint, burn, and ownership transfer—giving developers and token projects more flexibility.
 - Alignment with the Cosmos ecosystem: By standardizing on Cosmos EVM, XRPL EVM can more easily integrate with other Cosmos SDK chains, IBC modules, and upcoming interoperability upgrades.

Read more here: https://x.com/Peersyst/status/1971139829145514317

proposals.title: Update EVM params to allow the deployment of https://github.com/Arachnid/deterministic-deployment-proxy
proposals.summary:
This governance proposal updates the chain’s evm and feemarket module parameters to enable deployment of the Deterministic Deployment Proxy (Arachnid).
It sets allow_unprotected_txs = true to permit legacy, pre-EIP155 (unprotected) transactions required by the proxy’s deployment flow.
It also reduces base_fee to 100 GWei to ensure the deployment transaction meets fee constraints.
No other EVM behavior or chain parameters are modified. Once passed, the proxy can be deployed and used for deterministic contract deployments across environments.

proposals.title: Add Atlas Staking validator
proposals.summary: Atlas Staking has been running an XRPL mainnet validator without issue since genesis. We're excited to finally have a proposal on-chain and respectfully ask to be added. Atlas strives to be the kind of validator that makes life easier for everyone in the set: we run a cautious, well‑tested setup (multi‑datacenter sentries, keys kept off internet‑facing hosts, strict access controls, and practical incident runbooks) so we can be a steady, predictable peer when the network is under stress. Over the last few years, foundations and core teams in other ecosystems have chosen to delegate to us after doing their own checks, and we’ve tried to repay that trust by showing up reliably and communicating clearly during upgrades and incidents. We are active governance participants on all chains we support, and have published a deep library of ecosystem primers and staking tutorials to help onboard network users. A “yes” on this proposal adds a teammate who will quietly share the load of keeping blocks moving, participate constructively in discussions, and help explain changes to users and builders in ways that reduce, not increase, the support burden for the rest of the validator set.

proposals.title: Update Consensus Block Max Gas
proposals.summary: During the genesis phase of mainnet deployments, the consensus parameters were not properly set. As a result, the provided configuration was overridden by default values from CometBFT.
